articles.title: Deadly Bike Race on Rajpur Road: Rapido Passenger Killed, 4 Youths Arrested After Shocking CCTV
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Four youths have been arrested in connection with a fatal crash during an alleged motorcycle race on Rajpur Road in Dehradun that led to the death of a bike taxi passenger, police said on Sunday.

body.html:
Four youths have been arrested in connection with a fatal crash during an alleged motorcycle race on Rajpur Road in Dehradun that led to the death of a bike taxi passenger, police said on Sunday.

The accused have been identified as Pranjal Ramola (22), Abhishek Badoni (21), Lokendra alias Lokesh Bijalwan (22) — all residents of Uttarkashi — and Sumit Rathauri (22) from Dehradun.

The incident occurred on Friday night near Aketa Hotel on Rajpur Road under the Dalanwala Police Station area. Police said the accused were allegedly racing their motorcycles and attempting to overtake each other at high speed on the busy road.

According to police, the victim Ankit Pal was travelling as a passenger on a bike taxi operated through the Rapido platform when two speeding motorcycles collided with the vehicle. The impact caused Pal and the bike taxi rider to fall on the road, leaving them seriously injured.

Both were rushed to Government Doon Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared Pal brought dead.

Police registered a case on Saturday based on a complaint filed by the victim’s mother, Usha Pal. During the investigation, CCTV footage from the area revealed that after the first motorcycle struck the Rapido bike, another motorcycle following closely behind ran over Pal while he was lying on the road.

During interrogation, the accused admitted they were competing to get ahead of one another. Police said the pillion riders were also encouraging the riders to increase speed. Officials added that excessive speed and poor visibility near the hotel contributed to the fatal crash.

Initially, a case of causing death by negligence was registered, but after reviewing the CCTV footage, police added charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Pramendra Singh Dobal, Senior Superintendent of Police, Dehradun, warned that strict action will be taken against those who endanger public safety by violating traffic rules.

articles.title: Chaos in JD(U) Office! Workers Smash Furniture as Nitish Kumar Quits Bihar CM Post for Rajya Sabha
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Tensions flared at the Janata Dal (United) office on Thursday (5 Feb 2026) after party workers vandalised the premises to protest against Nitish Kumar stepping down as Chief Minister of Bihar. Angry supporters assembled outside the party office, raising slogans and damaging property.

body.html:
Tensions flared at the Janata Dal (United) office on Thursday (5 Feb 2026) after party workers vandalised the premises to protest against Nitish Kumar stepping down as Chief Minister of Bihar.

Angry supporters assembled outside the party office, raising slogans and damaging property. Furniture was smashed and utensils were broken, leaving the office in disarray. A video showing broken plates and toppled furniture from the premises has since gone viral on social media.

The protest erupted just before Kumar, the JD(U) supremo, was scheduled to file his nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha elections. The development comes barely four months after he began his record 10th term as Bihar’s Chief Minister last November.

Kumar filed his nomination on Thursday alongside Nitin Nabin, the national president of the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Confirming his move to the Upper House, the JD(U) leader said he would continue supporting the new government in Bihar. In a post on X, Kumar said he intends to become a member of the Rajya Sabha and assured that his commitment to working for a “developed Bihar” will remain unchanged.

While the party has not officially named his successor, political circles believe the move could pave the way for a BJP leader to head the NDA government in the state.

articles.title: Holi Turns Bloody: Husband Kills Estranged Wife, Throws Acid on Her Live-in Partner in Shahjahanpur
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 31-year-old woman was allegedly murdered by her estranged husband, who also threw acid on her live-in partner during a violent attack on Holi morning in the Chowk Kotwali area of Shahjahanpur.

body.html:
A 31-year-old woman was allegedly murdered by her estranged husband, who also threw acid on her live-in partner during a violent attack on Holi morning in the Chowk Kotwali area of Shahjahanpur.

The deceased has been identified as Aarti, who had been living in Balaji Nagar Colony with her partner Brijdeep for the past six months after separating from her husband, Manmohan Pandey.

According to Brijdeep’s complaint, the incident occurred around 6 am on Wednesday. Manmohan allegedly arrived at the house wearing a mask and knocked on the door. When Brijdeep opened the gate, the accused pushed his way inside and first threw gulal into his eyes before pouring acid on his face, causing serious burns.

Hearing his screams, Aarti rushed outside and allegedly tried to stop Manmohan by attacking him with a brick. However, the accused chased her, caught her, and s** her throat with a sharp weapon, killing her on the spot.

During the struggle, Brijdeep also hit Manmohan with a brick, leaving him seriously injured. After the attack, Aarti was found bleeding heavily while Brijdeep went inside to retrieve his phone and informed the police and family members.

Police rushed to the spot and shifted the injured men to the Government Medical College. Aarti was declared dead, while Manmohan remains in critical condition and Brijdeep is undergoing treatment for acid burns.

Police said Aarti and Manmohan had married about 10 years ago and have a seven-year-old daughter. Due to frequent disputes, Aarti had filed for divorce two years ago, and the couple were living separately.

Investigators said Aarti had been working as a data feeder under Brijdeep and the two were planning to marry soon, which allegedly angered Manmohan.

Based on Brijdeep’s complaint, police have registered a case and launched an investigation into the incident.

articles.title: Grandmother Allegedly Pours Boiling Water on 4-Year-Old in Koradi
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A four-year-old boy sustained severe burn injuries after his grandmother allegedly poured boiling water on him in the Koradi area of Nagpur district, police said on Wednesday. The incident took place on March 3 in Ward No. 2 of the Aramshin area and was captured on CCTV.

body.html:
A four-year-old boy sustained severe burn injuries after his grandmother allegedly poured boiling water on him in the Koradi area of Nagpur district, police said on Wednesday.

The incident took place on March 3 in Ward No. 2 of the Aramshin area and was captured on CCTV.

According to police, Om Harish Wange (4) was playing outside his house with a spray bottle filled with paint. He allegedly sprayed paint accidentally on his grandmother, identified as Sindhu Thackeray, who was filling a bucket with water heated on Holi wood.

Enraged by the act, she allegedly poured the boiling water on the child.

Om suffered serious scalding injuries below the waist and was rushed to a private hospital in Nagpur. Doctors have estimated that he sustained around 45 per cent burn injuries.

Police have initiated the process of registering an offence against the accused woman. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Two Accused in Attack on Ex-Muslim YouTuber Killed in Encounters in Ghaziabad district
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Police have stated that the two men accused of attacking social media activist Salim Wastik were killed in separate encounters on March 2 and March 4. Both carried a reward of ₹1 lakh each. Salim Wastik, whose real name is Salim Ahmed, is a resident of the Loni area in Ghaziabad district.

body.html:
Police have stated that the two men accused of attacking social media activist Salim Wastik were killed in separate encounters on March 2 and March 4. Both carried a reward of ₹1 lakh each.

Salim Wastik, whose real name is Salim Ahmed, is a resident of the Loni area in Ghaziabad district. He had been active on YouTube for the past few years and described himself as an ex-Muslim. He was reportedly attacked by two men wearing kurta-pajama. According to investigators, both suspects had blood stains on their clothes. Forensic examination also detected blood marks on a glass door handle at the scene.

Salim, who sustained injuries in the attack, was immediately taken to Delhi by family members and staff. He remains admitted to hospital.

Police said a key breakthrough came from a video recorded by a passerby, showing two men fleeing on a motorcycle with visible blood stains on their kurtas. Using the bike’s registration number, investigators scanned hundreds of CCTV cameras to trace the suspects’ movements and identify their residence and associates.

The first accused, identified as Zeeshan, was killed in a police encounter on March 2. His brother, Gulfam, was killed in a separate encounter on March 4. Police said both were residents of Amroha and were staying in Khoda Colony for work. Officials added that neither had any previous criminal record.

According to police sources, the brothers had allegedly conducted reconnaissance for nearly 20 days, tracking Salim’s daily routine before executing the attack during morning hours when he was alone.

Investigators are also probing possible ideological motives behind the crime. Salim had publicly criticised certain religious practices in his online content and had claimed conversion to Hinduism in recent years.

Police said further investigation is underway to examine all aspects of the case.

articles.title: Loco Pilot Undresses Before Senior Over Sick Leave Denial in Lucknow Rail Division
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A controversy has erupted in the Lucknow Rail Division after a loco pilot allegedly undressed before a senior officer to show his unhealed surgical wounds when his request for extension of medical leave was reportedly denied.

body.html:
A controversy has erupted in the Lucknow Rail Division after a loco pilot allegedly undressed before a senior officer to show his unhealed surgical wounds when his request for extension of medical leave was reportedly denied.

According to leaders of the All India Loco Running Staff Association (AILRSA), loco pilot Rajesh Meena, who underwent piles surgery on February 22 in Lucknow, was initially granted leave from February 22 to February 28. However, when his condition did not improve, he sought an extension as per procedure.

Union leaders said Meena approached the Railway Health Unit, where a doctor examined him and reportedly advised him to obtain a “sick memo” from his seniors. He then met the crew controller and Chief Crew Controller (CCC) Ratan Kumar for the required approval.

AILRSA alleged that despite producing medical documents, lab reports, prescriptions, and showing bandages and dressings, Meena’s request for rest leave was not accepted. In a video that has since circulated among railway employees’ WhatsApp groups, Meena and his colleagues are seen confronting the officer. The union claims that in desperation, Meena removed his trousers to display his unhealed wound.

“It is shameful that a loco pilot had to take such a step to seek medical leave,” said K.C. James, Secretary General of AILRSA. Adarsh Kumar Gupta, Assistant Secretary General (Northern Zone), stated that the union has demanded strict action against the CCC.

The union further said that Meena later approached a community union leader, following which senior officers intervened and he was reportedly granted rest leave.

No immediate response was received from Sunil Kumar Verma, Divisional Railway Manager of the Northern Railway, Lucknow Division.

The matter has triggered widespread discussion among railway staff, with the union terming the alleged treatment as inhuman. Further developments are awaited.

articles.title: CCTV Shows Youth Falling into Open Drain Near Agam Kuan Overbridge; Major Tragedy Averted
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A young man narrowly escaped a serious accident after falling into an open roadside chamber near the Agam Kuan Overbridge in Patna on the night of March 2, 2026. The incident occurred around 8 p.m.

body.html:
A young man narrowly escaped a serious accident after falling into an open roadside chamber near the Agam Kuan Overbridge in Patna on the night of March 2, 2026.

The incident occurred around 8 p.m. on NMCH Road, near RMRI Ganga Medical College, under the limits of the Alamganj Police Station. CCTV footage of the incident has gone viral on social media.

The footage shows the youth losing balance while getting off his bicycle and suddenly falling into an uncovered roadside drain chamber. The unexpected fall created panic among bystanders.

Local residents immediately rushed to his aid and launched a rescue operation. With considerable effort, they managed to pull him out safely. According to eyewitnesses, a major tragedy was averted due to the prompt response of locals. The young man’s condition is reported to be stable.

Following the incident, the area was temporarily cordoned off and several danger signs were installed.

Satyam Sahay, Sub-Divisional Officer of Patna City, stated that the administration acted swiftly to secure the site and alert the public about the open chamber.

The incident has raised concerns over civic negligence, with residents alleging that several drain covers remain open across different parts of the city. They claim such hazards pose a constant threat to pedestrians and commuters, particularly during the monsoon when waterlogging can conceal open drains.

articles.title: Woman Tied to Electric Pole Over Child-Lifting Rumour in Amroha
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident was reported from the Changa Darwaza locality under the Kotwali area of Amroha, where a mob allegedly tied a woman to an electric pole after mistaking her for a child thief. The incident took place around 10 pm on Tuesday (4 March 2026) night.

body.html:
A shocking incident was reported from the Changa Darwaza locality under the Kotwali area of Amroha, where a mob allegedly tied a woman to an electric pole after mistaking her for a child thief.

The incident took place around 10 pm on Tuesday (4 March 2026) night. According to reports, the woman was tied with a rope and publicly assaulted. Hundreds of people gathered at the spot, many recording videos, while the woman screamed for help. No immediate attempt was made by bystanders to rescue her.

On receiving information, police reached the scene, rescued the woman from the mob, and took her into custody. A video of the incident has since surfaced on social media.

Police are currently questioning the woman and investigating the entire matter to ascertain the facts. The incident has raised serious concerns over mob vigilantism and people taking the law into their own hands.

The Amroha Police stated that the Station House Officer of Amroha Nagar has been directed to take necessary legal action in connection with the case. Authorities are preparing to identify and act against those involved in tying and assaulting the woman.

articles.title: Wedding Night Turns into Crime Drama in Hathras: Bride’s Viral Video Adds New Twist
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A sensational case from Hathras district in Uttar Pradesh has taken a dramatic turn after a viral video surfaced of a bride accused of attacking her husband on their wedding night and fleeing with valuables.

body.html:
A sensational case from Hathras district in Uttar Pradesh has taken a dramatic turn after a viral video surfaced of a bride accused of attacking her husband on their wedding night and fleeing with valuables.

The woman, identified as Monika from Parsara village under Chandpa area, married Sunil Kumar of Nai Ka Nagla under the limits of Sadar Kotwali Police Station on February 21, 2026. She reached her matrimonial home on February 22.

According to the groom’s complaint, during the wedding night, Monika allegedly attacked him with a knife when he approached her, injuring his hand and warning him to stay away, claiming she loved someone else. He informed his family the next day.

The family further alleged that on February 25 evening, Monika prepared food allegedly laced with sedatives, causing family members to fall unconscious. She then fled with a relative identified as Sugriv, reportedly taking gold jewellery worth around ₹10 lakh, silver ornaments valued at ₹4–5 lakh, and ₹18,000 in cash — totalling approximately ₹15 lakh.

However, in a 1-minute-21-second video that has gone viral, Monika has denied the allegations of stabbing and theft. She has made serious counter-allegations, claiming she was forcibly married and that her father had confined and sold her for ₹8 lakh. She has also accused her uncle and father of *** assault. In the video, she states that she left home due to continuous harassment and has expressed fear for her life and that of her uncle.

Police said they have traced her location through mobile phone records. She has reportedly informed authorities that the marriage was against her will and has agreed to appear for questioning. Officials stated that both sides will be examined and the authenticity of the claims made in the viral video is being verified.

The investigation is ongoing.
